seal.statement: The rule set is governed by a sealed manifest rather than by a count. The manifest declares one entry per independently violable invariant, each naming exactly one owner key, and rules.md carries exactly one body per entry; the number of entries is derived from the manifest and is never the criterion, no always-load document states it, and growing the set requires a revision that names the predecessor revision, the published head it supersedes and a reason. The compound rule found at c0670a2af is split: R16 keeps the scope invariant its existing owner enforces, and the authorization invariant becomes R26 routed to what genuinely enforces the authorization boundary, with the absence of a single owner recorded as a gap rather than papered over. The evidence for the split is bounded and stated as what it is: the two invariants are decided by two real mechanisms whose parameter shapes are disjoint, so neither verdict can move with the other's input; the modelled table agrees with what those mechanisms do; and the two rules resolve to owners that share no authority. That the rule texts state two invariants rather than one is a semantic judgement, made by an independent verifier and recorded, not a property any checker can measure, because a rule may not name the implementation that decides it. Every property the previous revision held survives.

text: Sealed the successor and closed the second round's residuals. The claim now matches the evidence: the scenarios measure that the two invariants are decided by mechanisms with disjoint parameter shapes, that the table agrees with those mechanisms and that the two rules share no authority, and the semantic reading of the two rule texts is recorded as the verifier's judgement rather than asserted as proved. The doneWhen covers all eighteen scenarios rather than thirteen. The count detector now allows for words between the number and the noun and reaches beyond thirty; a revision must name a forty-hex published head and state truthfully how many entries its predecessor sealed; the rules preamble no longer names a file. Both the superseded quest and its successor keep producible receipts, drawn from one shared claim table after the two harnesses tripped the duplication ratchet as near-duplicates.

Correcting entry. Four earlier findings on this quest and its predecessor recorded only the word evidence or decision as their whole text: solve.js note takes the text as the value of --finding and the category as --kind, and I passed the category to --finding and the text to a --text flag the verb does not read. The entries stand as recorded; the content follows in the entries after this one. The same mistake dropped a finding on the closed steering-diet quest recording that the epic's authorizes list was widened from architecture/contracts to architecture plus CHANGELOG.md and DEBUGGING.md; that quest is terminal and takes no entries, but the widening and its reason are written into solve/epics/solve-v2.md, so nothing about it is lost.

Owner investigation of the authorization boundary at c0670a2af, carried forward from the superseded quest where its text was lost. There is no single owner. publish-head.js requires --fixes-red to equal the current origin/main SHA and a non-empty --reason before a red-main push, and requires --runner self-hosted to pair bidirectionally with a marker in the already-reviewed commit message, but it performs the push itself and an ordinary publish onto a green branch needs no signal at all. The pre-push hook refuses a main push while the newest completed CI run is red and fails open when it cannot reach CI. red-main-exemption.js keys acknowledgements to an exact SHA but accepts a missing reason and clears every record when given no argument. guards.js epicScopeProblems refuses any path outside the epic's sealed authorizes globs and is the only declarative authority grant in the repository. Behind no operator signal whatever: npm publish to the public registry, gh release upload --clobber of shared evidence, cloud host provisioning triggered by a config key, docker rm -f in the stat gate, and a release tag push, which skips the pre-push gate outright. Nothing refuses a force push; that is true only because no code performs one.

Independent verifier judgement on the split, recorded because no checker can measure it. Reading R16 and R26 as written, the verifier judged them two invariants rather than one: pushing a fully in-scope change violates R26 and not R16, and editing an unauthorised path locally violates R16 with no outward action at all, so neither entails the other. It also established the limit of the measured evidence: the scenarios show two functions with disjoint parameter shapes have independent outputs, which is a property of their signatures, and the step from mechanism to rule rests on the choice of decider, since a rule may not name the implementation that decides it. Two counterfeit R26 bodies restating the scope invariant were shown to pass every scenario. The measured part is that the two deciders are structurally blind to each other's input, that the modelled table agrees with them, and that the two rules resolve through the router to files that share nothing.

Two records the second verification asked for, re-entered after the text was lost. The receipt of the closed steering-diet quest names the command solve-v2-budget.js --metric rules-md-count beside a passed flag; this revision replaced that metric, so the command now exits 1 while the frozen receipt keeps reading green. The receipt is sealed evidence bound to c0670a2af, stays byte-identical, and this is the record that its command no longer resolves. Separately, the always-load transitive path is 349 lines of 360: the next rule will not fit without moving something out of that layer first.

Third adversarial verification. Approved. The verifier confirmed the supersession was applied correctly rather than the failed claim being reworded into a true one: the predecessor's quest.json is unmodified and still contains the word proved, its log grew only by the rejection and the terminal entry, and the append-only audit is clean. It read the new statement sentence by sentence against the eighteen receipts and found each measured, noting two remaining tensions it accepts: the rule-to-mechanism binding is measured only to file granularity, and one entry per independently violable invariant is asserted across all twenty-six while being unmeasurable for the pair anyone examined. It verified independently, with a wider pattern than the checker's, that no always-load document states a count today. Three mechanical defects were then fixed: my own findings had recorded only their category because I passed the text to a flag the verb does not read, so the content is re-entered after a correcting entry and the supersession is now a named field rather than prose; the count detector scanned line by line and missed a count written across a hard wrap or around bold markup, the likeliest way for one to reappear, and now reads the document with markup and wrapping removed; and receiptsFor silently dropped an unknown claim id, the same permissive-selection shape fixed in the budget one round earlier, and now throws.
